sections.heading: C2 — Driving records, suspensions and reinstatement
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Driving records, suspensions and reinstatement

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A126
An ALS is a civil sanction separate from criminal court penalties; its requirements do not remove the duty to attend the scheduled DUI court appearance. [A126]
Source: [A126 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A126
The handbook makes the suspension notice effective thirty days after service, meaning receipt of the notice. [A126]
Source: [A126 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A126
For a first evidentiary-test failure, the handbook gives a ninety-day suspension with no driving during its first thirty days. [A126]
Source: [A126 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A126
After that first-failure suspension ends, the source requires an ignition interlock on any vehicle driven for one year. [A126]
Source: [A126 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A126
A second evidentiary-test failure within five years carries a one-year suspension allowing no driving privileges. [A126]
Source: [A126 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A126
The handbook's implied-consent description covers a person driving or physically controlling a vehicle when suspected of impaired driving, for an alcohol or drug test under the stated law. [A126]
Source: [A126 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A126
Refusing an officer-requested evidentiary test subjects the person to the described suspension and a two-hundred-fifty-dollar civil penalty. [A126]
Source: [A126 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A126
For the described first refusal, an officer issues a notice and a court's upholding the findings leads to a one-year absolute suspension. [A126]
Source: [A126 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A127
A second test refusal within ten years brings a two-year absolute suspension in addition to any DUI-conviction penalty. [A127]
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A127
A person with a suspended Idaho license may qualify for a restricted permit for travel such as work or medical treatment. [A127]
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A127
For a department suspension, apply to the department in Boise for the described restricted permit; for a court suspension, apply to the convicting court. [A127]
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A127
The handbook says interlocks are mandatory after administrative suspensions end; a DUI conviction also requires an interlock in any driven vehicle unless the court orders otherwise. [A127]
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-R13 | anchor: A127
An ignition interlock requires a starting breath sample and prevents engine start when alcohol reaches or exceeds its preset level. [A127]
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-R14 | anchor: A127
The driver pays interlock installation, maintenance and recurring monthly charges. [A127]
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-R15 | anchor: A127
After a suspension or revocation period ends, the handbook describes applying to the department for restoration of privileges. [A127]
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec15-R16 | anchor: A127
The printed reinstatement-fee range is twenty-five through two hundred eighty-five dollars depending on the suspension; multiple suspensions may require multiple fees. [A127]
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0127]

ranked.label: Recognize conditional permits and interlock rules
Treat reinstatement as a conditional process

corpus_stability.reason: Corpus is the frozen July handbook snapshot; future issuer changes require a new source registration, rather than silent updates to this corpus.

verification_debt.claim_text: The ALS, refusal, court-review and interlock rules on physical pages one hundred twenty-five through one hundred twenty-seven need current legal verification, including the blanket all-ALS interlock wording and interaction with absolute suspensions. Source conditions are preserved; no broader eligibility is inferred.

The reinstatement paragraph on physical page one hundred twenty-seven ends mid-sentence and continues onto one hundred twenty-eight. Applying and paying source-described fees do not constitute a complete reinstatement checklist; the continuation needs a supported multi-page binding.

The handbook's twenty-five-through-two-hundred-eighty-five-dollar reinstatement range and possible multiple fees are not verified against a current official schedule. Do not quote a current payable amount or guarantee restoration from payment alone.
